Minutes of the Meeting to deliberate on Tripping of 400 kV Transmission Lines of Mumbai 
Area on 30-31 July, 2025:
1. An on-line meeting was held under the chairmanship of Member (Power Systems), CEA on  
04.08.2025 at 11:30   hrs  to deliberate  on the  tripping of  400 kV Transmission Lines  
feeding Mumbai Area on 30-31 July, 2025. List of participants is given at Annexure-I.
2. At the outset, Member (Power Systems), CEA welcomed all the participants and briefed  
about the agenda of the meeting. He informed  that the matter regarding tripping of the  
following  three  transmission  Lines  feeding  power  to  Mumbai  area,  occurred  on  
30.07.2025/31.07.2025 was apprised in the HMOP meeting held on 01.08.2025.
a. 400 kV Phadge -Navi Mumbai S/C line
b. 400 kV Phadge- Kharghar S/C line
c. 400 kV Navi Mumbai-Vikhroli S/C line
He stated that tripping of the above lines is stated to be due to large no. of Insulator  
failures. As these lines have been commissioned recently, failure of so many Insulators is  
a matter of concern. As any further tripping of lines feeding to Mumbai may lead to  
precarious situation of large-scale interruption of Power Supply, efforts shall be made to  
restore the above lines on priority basis. Failure of the insulator shall be analyzed by the  
Standing Committee on the Tower failure/ PSE&TD Division, CEA. 
3. He requested WRPC, WRLDC and M/s Resonia (MUML-Sterlite), and M/s Adani  (KVTPL-
Adani) to explain the issues relating to tripping of the above Lines and reasons for failure  
of large no. of Insulators within short span of time from their commissioning, along with  
measures taken to restore them. 
4. Representative of WRLDC made a presentation, and the following were highlighted:
a) 400 kV Padghe (PG)-Kharghar S/c tripped on R-N fault at 03:45 hrs of 30.07.025. 400  
kV Padghe(PG)-Navi Mumbai S/c tripped on B-N fault at 12:15 hrs of 30.07.2025 and  
400 kV Navi Mumbai – Vikhroli S/c on Y-N fault at 03:24 hrs of 31.07.2025. These  
lines tripped due to failure of insulators. While the ownership of the first two lines is  
with MUML-Sterlite, that of the third line is with both MUML-Sterlite and KVTPL-
Adani. However, the Insulator failures portion belongs to MUML-Sterlite. And all the  
three lines were commissioned in September, 2024
b) Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) area is fed mainly from the seven (7) numbers  
400 kV lines and 2x315 MVA + 2x500 MVA, 400/220 kV Boisar ICTs. During tripping  
of above lines in MMR area, the remaining feed was through following elements:  
 400 kV Padghe (MH)-Kalwa-D/c lines (HTLS)  
 400 kV Pune (PG)-Kharghar-S/c (Twin Moose)  
 400 kV Pune (PG)-Vikhroli-S/c (Twin Moose)  
 2x315 MVA + 2x500 MVA, 400/220 kV Boisar ICTs
c) Due to tripping of the said 400 kV lines, the loading on the above elements were  
significantly increased. Further, drawl of MMR from the grid also observed to have  
exceeded  its  ATS  limit  of  1690  MW.  To  manage  the  situation,  the  internal/ 
embedded generation from with MMR had been maximized (1877 MW) to cater to  
MMR’s load.

d) From  the  meetings  they  held  with  Sterlite  on  31.07.2025,  01.08.2025,  and 
02.08.2025, it was noted that all the failed insulators are of Tag make, and were  
from manufacturing batch of December, 2022 and July, 2023.
e) As additional precautionary measures, the following have also been done:
 MSLDC  has  been  instructed  to  identify  areas  for  manual  load  shedding,  in 
addition to existing LTS (Load Trimming Scheme), to control transmission line  
loadings under stressed conditions.
 MSLDC/ MSETCL has proposed to take load on 2x500 MVA, 400/220 kV Kudus  
(MH) ICTs to create  an alternate  supply path from Padghe (PG) → Kudus  →  
Borivali (Mumbai). This is to be implemented through an interim arrangement of  
220 kV Kudus–Borivali-2, by cross-jumpering 220 kV Kudus–Ghodbunder and 220  
kV Ghodbunder–Borivali lines, effectively bypassing Ghodbunder. Load taken on  
2x500 MVA, 400/220 kV ICTs at 02:56hrs & 02:58hrs of 03-08-2025 respectively  
after  implementation  of  interim  arrangement.  However,  hotspot  on  220  kV 
Kudus-Borivali-2 (interim arrangement) was observed. 400/220 kV Kudus ICTs  
also hand tripped at 10:58hrs/03-08-2025 for controlling the loading on 220 kV  
Kudus-Borivali-1. 
f) As on 04.08.2025, 400 kV Phadge- Kharghar line was restored (charged) at 10.01 hrs  
of 04.08.2025. And the remaining two lines were also expected to be to restored/  
charged by 04.08.2025.
g) The preliminary report furnished by Grid-India/ WRLDC in this regard is at Annexure-
II.
5. Representative of MUML-Sterlite informed that tripping of the lines was due to the failure  
of the insulators. He informed that 45 Nos. insulator had been replaced in the 400 kV  
Phadge- Kharghar line; 50 Nos. Insulators (30 failed and 20 suspected) had been replaced  
in the 400 kV Phadge -Navi Mumbai line; and 13 Nos Insulators had been replaced and 8  
Nos. insulators to be replaced in the 400 kV Navi Mumbai-Vikhroli line. He also informed  
that sample of the failed insulator was also sent to ERDA for testing, and waiting the test  
results.
He also informed that 400 kV Phadge- Kharghar S/C line had been restored by 10 hrs on  
04.08.2025. The 400 kV Phadge -Navi Mumbai S/C line was expected to be restored by  
12:00 hrs on 04.08.2025, and 400 kV Navi Mumbai-Vikhroli S/C line was expected to be  
restored by late night of 04.08.2025. 
6. Representative of the M/s Adani confirmed that there were no failure of insulators in their  
line. 
7. In this regard, Chief Engineer (PSE&TD), CEA stated the following:
 As so many Insulators (Long-rod Polymer type) were observed to have failed within  
two years of their manufacturing, the concerned Utilities/ Line Owners should take up  
the issue with their OEMs, and review the Quality Assurance Plan (QAP) with focus on  
Insulators  being  followed  by  them  with  the  OEMs.  As  the  failed  Insulators  were 
observed to be of same (‘Tag’) make from manufacturing batch of December, 2022  
and  July,  2023,  he  requested  to  collect  details  regarding  supplying  of  the  same 
lot/batch  Insulators  to  other  utilities  so  that  corrective  action  including  their

replacement may be taken up. On this, WRPC confirmed that the same had already  
been initiated by them, and would be getting the requisite details within a week time. 
 In this regard, he briefed about the Model Quality Assurance Plan (MQAP) Guidelines  
issued by CEA in March, 2022, and requested all concerned (Utilities and OEMs) to  
adhere  to  them.  He  also  detailed  the  regulatory  requirements  w.r.t.  Insulators, 
including the requirement of maintaining a minimum specific creepage distance 31  
mm/ kV (as per IS 16683: Part-I: 2018). MUML-Sterlite, KVTPL-Adani, PGCIL confirmed  
their compliance w.r.t. the same.
 He also stated that, as suggested by Member (PS), CEA, the above Insulator Failure  
events  would be  discussed in the  forthcoming meeting  of  Standing  Committee  of 
Experts on Tower Failures, and requested MUML-Sterlite furnish details as per the  
format  given  at
Annexure-III.
 He also flagged the issue of several forced outages in MMR and South Gujarat during  
the  period  from  30-07-2025  to  02-08-2025,  resulting  in  emergency  operating 
conditions.  Some  13  Nos.  of  lines  belonging  to  GETCO,  PGCIL  &  MSETCL  were 
observed to have got tripped, out of which some events were observed to be due to  
Insulator failures. He requested concerned Utilities to take preventive O&M of the  
lines regularly, and ensure their availability during critical times such as above. 
 W.r.t.  MSLDC/ MSETCL’s failed attempt of providing  alternate supply path through  
Padghe (PG) → Kudus → Borivali (Mumbai) from 220 kV side, he emphasized on the  
need for regular O&M of substation equipment and transmission lines so that timey  
detection of weak links & hot spots is ensured, and corrective action is taken in time. 
The meeting ended with thanks to the Chair.

 Brief on  Unified Real Time Dynamic State Measurement  URTDSM Project Phase-II  for discussion in RPCs   1.0 Background of URTDSM Phase-II Proposal:  POWERGRID has been entrusted to prepare the DPR for URTDSM Phase-II project in the 13th NPC meeting held on 05.07.2023. The DPR is to be made on basis of ‘Report of the Sub-Committee on PMU Placement and Analytics under URTDSM Phase II’ constituted by National Power Committee.   Presently 1400 PMUs and 32 Control centres have been established under the URTDSM Phase-I project. This project was implemented with 70% of the project cost as PSDF grant and 30% was through POWERGRID Equity (RTM for 30% portion and no tariff for 70% grant portion).   Similarly, DPR for URTDSM Phase-II Project, which included 4000PMUs(new) and 34 control centres was prepared with funding pattern of 70% PSDF grant and 30% POWERGRID equity in line with Phase-I. The DPR, with an estimate of Rs.3922 Crores, was submitted to NPC/CEA on 11.03.2024. The scope included replacement of 34 control centres and supply of 4000 new PMUs including integration of 1400 existing PMUs.  In the 14th NPC meeting held in Bengaluru on 03.02.2024, DPR status was updated to members. It was suggested to optimize the cost. Further, NPC vide email dated 18.04.2024 has informed that PSDF funding shall not be available for the project and alternate sources of funding shall be explored by POWERGRID. Hence, POWERGRID approached all the Constituents in the RPCs for concurrence for execution of the URTDSM Phase-II Project on RTM basis.  In the 15th NPC Meeting held on 14.11.2024, the committee recommended that “PowerGrid is to submit the revised proposal in consultation with Grid India, only for the existing network after segregating the PMUs and control centers under ISTS and STUs system. The proposal may also be revised to optimize the number of control centers and PMUs at ISTS & STUs system separately. The revised proposal for ISTS portion may be put up to the NCT for further consideration.”  During previous NPC & RPC meetings for URTDSM phase-II project, it was discussed that the number of PMUs for URTDSM Phase-II need to be optimized for reducing the overall project cost. The initial DPR prepared by POWERGRID was based on the sub-committee recommended philosophy of PMU placement. However, CEA has published new guidelines for unified philosophy of PMU placement in Indian Grid in March 2025, which will supersede all existing guidelines and sub-committee report etc.,   According to 15th NPC, POWERGRID was entrusted to put up proposal for ISTS portion to NCT and revised proposal for ISTS and STU portion separately for discussion. ISTS portion comprises of Control Centers of Grid-India (NLDCs and RLDCs) and PMUs for Central Sector locations as per latest CEA Guidelines referred above.  POWERGRID prepared DPR for URTDSM Phase-II ISTS portion (upgradation of control centers at NLDCs, RLDCs and installation of new PMUs for Central Sector stations as per latest CEA guidelines). Tentative cost and BOQ for STUs portion (Control centers of SLDCs across India and new PMUs for State sector substations) is also put up for discussion in the 16th NPC.   Upon the concurrence of 16th NPC for proposed DPR for ISTS portion, the same will be put up to NCT for approval in RTM route. For the State Sector, funding methodology is to be finalized in reference to the tentative cost and BOQ.

 2.0 Brief Details of URTDSM Phase-I Project:  POWERGRID took up the implementation of URTDSM phase-1 in Jan 2014 and the project was commissioned progressively from 2018 to 2021 with installation of 1409 PMUs and PDCs at 32 control centers, the project was funded 70% from PSDF grant and 30% from POWERGRID equity.  The existing system of URTDSM Phase-I is under maintenance support through Annual Maintenance contract with the contractor, which will end in Jan 2027. The PMUs installed at substations can be in service for fifteen years from their date of commissioning.  3.0 Need for URTDSM Phase-II Project  3.1 Need for new PMUs  After commissioning of URTDSM Phase-I Scheme, expansion of power system has taken place at considerable pace with addition of large-scale renewable generation and incorporation of new transmission system technologies (SVC, STATCOM, FSC, etc.,). Over the years, there have been significant organizational, regulatory, Market operations, and technological changes. The placement of PMUs at new renewable generation plants and other new technology devices (FACTS) is required to know their dynamic response during disturbances and to verify that they are operating under the limits stipulated as per the regulatory norms.   The Committee report on PMU has defined a new philosophy for placement of PMUs and suggested to cover additional equipment such as ICTs, SVCs, Bus Reactors, FSC, TCSC etc. have been considered for measurement through PMU, which were not in Phase-I implementation.   3.2 Upgradation of Control centers  AMC support for the existing control centers will lapse by Jan 2027. Due to this, the maintenance of the existing hardware and software beyond its design life cycle of 7 years will be very challenging owing to lack of spares and services, poor performance and increasing cyber vulnerabilities due to obsolete technologies.  Moreover, the existing hardware and software cannot support the new analytics being envisaged under Phase-II project for better monitoring of the power system.  The URTDSM phase-1 Control centres are having issues of End of Life/End of support due to technical obsolescence of software, hardware, and cyber security appliances and will become technically obsolete. Hence to keep the WAMS URTDSM Control centres functional, the URTDSM phase 2 project which includes the upgrade of existing control centres, is to be implemented on priority.  Increased penetration of Renewable energy has required increase in more monitoring of the regional grids which requires more deployment of PMUs. The URTDSM phase 2 includes installation of PMUs as per latest CEA Guidelines on PMU placement.  3.3 Additional technical factors to establish the need for URTDSM Phase-II System  In addition to the reasons mentioned above, the following are some of the power system aspects which are being handled only with URTDSM system, which is based upon Wide Area Measurement System (WAMS) technology:  (i) PMU measurements provide synchronized voltage, current and phase angle measurements, which is not possible in RTU measurements. The phase angle measurement is valuable information about the state of the grid and the grid operators can take decisions based upon precise measured information instead of thumb rule based upon their experience.  (ii)  Based upon the phase angle measurements from both the ends of the line enhanced utilization of Transmission lines closer to thermal loading of line can be achieved.

(iii) In case of system separations, the Synchrophasor measurements display the load angle separation and can be used to determine the change required in generation to synchronize the two isolated systems, this being more accurate data facilitates faster restoration and avoid any jerks or oscillations in the power system.
